subject: Warmup starvation & burst throttling — remediation timeline + evidence pack
thread_body:
--- Message 1 (initial report) ---
From: Tom Roberts <tom.roberts@datasentry.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Sudden tail latency spike + warmup failures in our reserved pool

Hi Vivek / Ben,

We observed a series of 95th/99th tail latency spikes starting ~08:47 UTC this morning against our dedicated pool (pool-id: dsny-east-3). A bunch of requests timed out or returned partial responses from our side — looks like model warmup was failing and the service then started shedding burst QPS. Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate (gpt-neo-x-30b), and some rerank jobs.

We attached a short monitoring snapshot to this thread. Can you confirm whether this is an autoscaler warmup starvation issue or a node-level eviction? We need to assess customer impact (SLOs) and get an ETA for a fix or workaround.

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead, DataSentry

Attachments: monitoring_snippet_20261201.png (image)

--- Message 2 (acknowledgement) ---
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Roberts <tom.roberts@datasentry.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:25:10Z
Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency spike + warmup failures in our reserved pool

Tom — thank you for the heads up and the snapshot. We’ve opened an ops investigation immediately and I’m looping in Ben and Marissa (on-call infra + CS lead).

Short answer: we’re seeing a warmup queue backlog and aggressive burst-rate throttles on that pool. We suspect a scheduler thrash combined with a GC/driver recycle on a subset of nodes; chasing evidence now. I’ll send an interim runbook and mitigation within the hour.

-Vivek

--- Message 3 (internal ops handoff) ---
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tom Roberts <tom.roberts@datasentry.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:37:45Z
Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency spike + warmup failures in our reserved pool

Marissa / Karthik — we have a live incident for DataSentry (pool dsny-east-3). Symptom set: warmup worker queue backlog, a ~40% drop in effective warmup throughput, and subsequent per-tenant burst throttling that returned 503s for short bursts.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: pull scheduler logs (scheduler-master and allocator) from 08:30–09:30 UTC, grep for warmup_eviction / warmup_backlog / preempt events.
- Marissa: prepare a short mitigation we can apply to this pool (increase warmup concurrency cap + disable aggressive burst circuit) and a rollback guard.
- Vivek: confirm commercial impact / whether DataSentry wants an immediate failover to a compatible hosted instance while we stabilize.

I’ll attach the first-pass evidence bundle to the external thread once we’ve collected logs.

- Ben

--- Message 4 (ops evidence share to customer) ---
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Roberts <tom.roberts@datasentry.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@datasentry.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, CloudOps Support <support@cloudops.io>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:02:03Z
Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency spike + warmup failures in our reserved pool

Hi Tom / Alice — quick update from the ops team below, plus a first-pass evidence bundle attached.

Summary of findings (interim):
- Root symptom: warmup worker queue thrash caused by a tight scheduler retry loop when a subset of warmup workers entered transient driver restarts (NVIDIA driver rebind during a rolling driver refresh).
- Effect: warmup throughput dropped ~38% for ~14 minutes (08:46–09:00 UTC) leading to queued warmup requests and subsequent short burst throttling.
- Mitigation applied (09:05 UTC): we temporarily increased warmup concurrency for dsny-east-3 and relaxed the burst circuit for your tenant. This removed the immediate backlog and reduced 99p latency to baseline within ~6 minutes.

What we attached: scheduler_logs_20261201.txt (traces from scheduler-master), node_journal_excerpt.txt (driver rebind traces), and a correlation graph. Evidence bundle: evidence_bundle_20261201.tar.gz.

Planned next steps:
1) Root cause postmortem (complete) by 2026-12-04 with recommended platform changes and a permanent scheduler patch.
2) A small SLO credit proposal commensurate with the 14-minute elevated tail (proposal attached).
3) Optional migration assistance to a hosted fallback pool for the next two weeks while we roll the scheduler patch if you prefer a guarded approach.

Tom — please let us know which next step you prefer (credit vs migration assistance vs both). We’ll also share the full postmortem when ready.

Attachments: scheduler_logs_20261201.txt (text), node_journal_excerpt.txt (text), evidence_bundle_20261201.tar.gz (archive)

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

--- Message 5 (customer acceptance + follow-up questions) ---
From: Tom Roberts <tom.roberts@datasentry.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@datasentry.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T12:10:32Z
Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency spike + warmup failures in our reserved pool

Thanks Marissa — that’s helpful and timely. We’d like the migration assistance to a hosted fallback while you ship the scheduler patch; please open the migration run (we’ll need traffic cutover windows and a short verification test). Also interested in the SLO credit: can you confirm the calculation basis (token counts vs request counts)?

Also, can you confirm whether our logs showed any model weight integrity issues or corrupted KV cache entries? We want to be sure there was no data exposure or inference corruption.

-Tom

--- Message 6 (final internal confirmation and next steps to customer) ---
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Roberts <tom.roberts@datasentry.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@datasentry.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, CloudOps Support <support@cloudops.io>
Date: 2026-12-04T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Warmup starvation & burst throttling — remediation timeline + evidence pack

Tom / Alice — following up with concrete answers and the completed short postmortem attached.

Key confirmations:
- No model weight corruption or KV cache incoherence observed — all hash checks and integrity verifications passed during our analysis. Your inference outputs show no signs of truncation beyond the partial responses caused by timeouts.
- SLO credit: attached PDF outlines our calculation (we apply request-count weighting for burst events and token-weighted for generation latency windows). Proposed credit: 3.5% of monthly committed spend for the affected window; details in SLO_credit_proposal_20261204.pdf.
- Migration runbook: we’ve created a scoped migration plan and scheduled a dry-run for 2026-12-06 02:00–03:00 UTC (off-peak). Link: https://redwood.app/drive/Shared/DSY-Evidence-20261201/migration-runbook.md. Ops will execute and share verification metrics.

Attached: postmortem_20261204.txt, SLO_credit_proposal_20261204.pdf.

If you approve the migration dry-run I’ll lock the window and send a short checklist (prep steps for your team). If you prefer only the credit, we’ll proceed with that and skip the migration.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Software Engineer, Platform Reliability

--- End of thread ---
